rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 18 September 2026 (Weekly) Executive Summary • 🟡 Hong Kong RMB market development: the 2026 Policy Address signals a seven-day offshore RMB liquidity tender mechanism, exploration of short-term RMB debt instruments, and encouragement for more foreign banks to join CIPS directly. Treasury and payments planning may need to assess funding, liquidity and connectivity dependencies once HKMA terms emerge; no new authorised-institution requirement or timetable is stated. • 🟡 UK cryptoasset perimeter benchmark: the FCA says its future-regime guidance addresses activities that may require authorisation, with applications opening on 30 September 2026 and the regime due to enter force on 25 October 2027. This is relevant to UK-facing activity mapping, not a Hong Kong requirement. Hong Kong 🟡 The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — International Financial Centre 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20260916-daily-exploratory-search-ca74866cbc ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: FX, investment, cross-border-GBA The 16 September Policy Address says the HKMA will introduce a tendering mechanism for seven-day offshore RMB liquidity to broaden banks’ short-term-financing channels. It also says the HKMA will explore offshore RMB short-term debt instruments for investment and liquidity management, and encourage more foreign banks in Hong Kong to join CIPS directly. This is Government policy and market-development direction, not a binding rule or HKMA supervisory guideline; the source states no timetable, eligibility, terms, reporting duty or participation condition. Treasury and payments teams may need to identify relevant RMB funding, investment and CIPS-connectivity dependencies as implementation details emerge, while formal HKMA terms remain the decision point. Source: The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address Mainland/GBA No qualifying current-run items. SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. 🟡 Crypto firms get guidance on how the new regime applies 🇬🇧 Item ID: item-20260916-fca-benchmark-crypto-guidance ⏰ Deadline: UK authorisation applications open 30 September 2026; UK regime enters force 25 October 2027; FCA consultation planned for October 2026 Products: investment, digital The FCA’s 16 September press release says new guidance explains how the law underpinning the future UK cryptoasset regime applies and which activities may require FCA authorisation. The stated activity categories include qualifying-stablecoin issuance, cryptoasset trading-platform operation, dealing or arranging, safeguarding, and arranging staking. The FCA says applications open on 30 September 2026, the regime enters force on 25 October 2027, and it plans an October consultation on targeted guidance updates following Government legal changes. This is a UK perimeter-development benchmark rather than a Hong Kong requirement; UK-facing cryptoasset activity may warrant entity, product, custody-provider and customer-journey mapping, while Hong Kong-only activity is not evidence of an HK control gap. Source: Crypto firms get guidance on how the new regime applies Primary source: official document Watch List • Monitor HKMA terms for the offshore RMB liquidity mechanism, short-term debt instruments and direct CIPS participation. • Monitor the FCA’s planned October 2026 consultation and assess any effect only where UK-facing activity is identified. Weekly Trend This week’s retained developments combine Hong Kong market-infrastructure direction with a UK cryptoasset-perimeter benchmark. The available sources point to preparation and monitoring decisions rather than a new binding Hong Kong requirement.
